conversation.content: Hi there—my name is Sarah, and I’m a perinatal mental-health clinician. I’m here to check in on how you’ve been feeling since your baby arrived. We’ll use a short, well-studied tool called the Edinburgh Postnatal Depression Scale (EPDS). It’s simply 10 questions about the past seven days; your answers help us see if you might benefit from extra emotional support or resources. Everything you share stays confidential within your care team, and this is a judgment-free space—no right or wrong answers, just whatever feels true for you. When you’re ready, I’ll ask the first question.
[Soft exhale] Okay… thanks, Sarah. I’m ready when you are.
I have been able to laugh and see the funny side of things
[Small shrug, eyes down] Lately… not really. I mean, maybe once or twice something felt a little funny, but mostly I just feel flat. It’s like the laughter doesn’t come easily anymore.
I have looked forward with enjoyment to things

I still get excited for a couple of small things—like when my sister drops off coffee or when I can sit outside for five minutes—but most of the time it feels like I’m just going through the motions. Nothing feels as enjoyable as it did before the baby.
I have blamed myself unnecessarily when things went wrong

Yeah… I do that. If the baby’s fussy or won’t settle, I automatically think it’s something I did—like I’m not feeding him right or I missed his cues. Even little stuff, like spilling a bottle, makes me feel I’m failing him.
I have been anxious or worried for no good reason

[Hands twist in lap] Pretty much every day. I’ll be sitting there and suddenly picture him stopping breathing, or I’ll worry I didn’t strap the car seat right. There’s no real reason—it just jumps into my head and then I can’t shake it for a while.
I have felt scared or panicky for no very good reason
Yes… a few times this week. It’s like my heart starts racing out of nowhere and I feel shaky, like something awful is about to happen, even when the baby’s asleep and everything’s quiet.
Things have been getting on top of me

Most days, yeah. It feels like the second I finish one thing—feeding, diapers, laundry—there’s already three more waiting. Sometimes I just sit on the couch staring at the mess thinking, “I can’t keep up,” but I still push through because I have to.
I have been so unhappy that I have had difficulty sleeping

It’s been hard to fall asleep several nights this week. My mind keeps spinning with all the “what-ifs” about the baby, and once I doze off I wake up once or twice with my heart pounding, then I lie there feeling sad and worried until I finally drift off again.
I have felt sad or miserable

Yeah… that’s pretty much how I feel most of the day. I wouldn’t say it’s every single second, but it’s like this heavy cloud that settles over me, and even when I’m doing something “normal” I still feel teary and low inside.
I have been so unhappy that I have been crying

[Voice drops] I’ve cried a couple of times this week—once when I couldn’t get him to nap and once after my mom left. It just hits me out of nowhere and I can’t stop the tears, even though I feel silly for crying over “nothing.”
The thought of harming myself has occurred to me

[Long pause, eyes flick to the floor] Once or twice… just a quick flash, like “what if I wasn’t here.” I don’t have any plan or real wish to do it—I could never leave my baby—but the thought did pop in, and it scared me.

postpartum depression screening impression for patient with EPDS score 23: Postpartum Depression / Anxiety Screening Note  
Date: [today]

Source: Patient self-report on EPDS-10 analogue interview, 3 wks post-delivery.

Symptoms endorsed:
- Persistent low mood, anhedonia, tearfulness (Q1, Q2, Q8, Q9)
- Marked guilt / self-blame regarding infant care (Q3)
- Daily, intrusive, “no-reason” worry and catastrophic images (Q4)
- Panicky surges, palpitations, shakiness (Q5)
- Feeling overwhelmed, inability to keep up with routine tasks (Q6)
- Sleep-onset and maintenance problems driven by rumination (Q7)

Pattern: Symptoms present most days and interfere with functioning.

Safety: Fleeting passive suicidal ideation (“what if I wasn’t here”), no plan or intent; patient finds thought ego-dystonic and reports protective factor of infant.

Risk factors: Primiparity, sleep deprivation, absence of perceived enjoyment, high self-criticism, comorbid anxiety.

Screening impression: High clinical concern for major depressive episode with anxious features; rule-out generalized anxiety disorder. Immediate safety plan reviewed; referral for expedited psychiatric evaluation and perinatal mental-health follow-up recommended.
